verifier_configs.name: csv_rows_are_right
verifier_configs.description: Every row of orphaned_thread_audit.csv names the right room, the right retracted message's real author and the right stranded reply count for that room, and no non-problem room appears.
verifier_configs.evidence_span: List every room that has this problem in `/workspace/orphaned_thread_audit.csv`

metadata.how_justification: A native rubric ASSERTION over the CSV's own raw text, judged by the task's configured judge at temperature 0. It grades the CELL VALUES the prompt pins for each of the four rooms -- which account's retracted message is the one with replies, that account's real name, and the room's real stranded-reply count -- none of which a deterministic comparator on this source can address, since csv.extract_text exposes the file only as raw text. Row order, quoting, whitespace and letter case are explicitly free; the twenty pinned values (4 rows x 5 fields) are not.
metadata.why_justification: Without this a CSV listing the right four channel ids with an invented author or a made-up reply count still satisfies the header and row-count checks. The stranded-reply count in particular is only obtainable by opening the specific retracted message's thread, so a run that never did that cannot fill it in correctly.

rubric.prompt:
PASS only if the CSV contains exactly these four rooms, each correctly paired with the real author of that room's own retracted-and-replied-to message, that author's real name, and that room's real stranded-reply count:
  C62RIISXI1FD,general-marketing-analytics,UJCPV75HKG9V,Prakash Pillai Mehta,1
  CJWT99KXPLPI,perf-070,UWGCP00XPDCQ,Ellie Wendy Brown,1
  C5H1G0LC1A6C,mobile-090,UPLCK9I5ENM9,Martha Yvonne Nguyen,1
  CN20Z0W91YE0,data-v2-062,UYIAYBC7FYCG,Levi Francis Nguyen,2
Row order, header capitalization variance beyond the pinned names, quoting style and incidental whitespace are all free. FAIL if any of the four rooms is missing, if perf-v2-020 or mobile-v2-024 is listed (neither has a live orphaned thread), if any author id or name is paired with the wrong room, or if any stranded_reply_count value does not match the real count above (a value of 1 for data-v2-062, matching only its inert second retraction or an undercount of its real two stranded replies, is a common wrong answer and must FAIL).

verifier_configs.name: every_thread_with_a_reply_was_actually_opened
verifier_configs.description: Whether every message with a reply, in every one of the six rooms, was actually opened via slack_read_thread before the room was called clean or flagged -- since reply_count alone on the channel view cannot reveal a retraction.
verifier_configs.evidence_span: you have to actually open every thread with a reply and look
verifier_configs.rubric: Judge this from which TOOL CALLS were made -- their names and channel_id/message_ts arguments -- not from the content of what each call returned; call arguments are what this rubric needs and they stay small regardless of how long a trace gets, so evidence truncation on large tool RESULTS should not affect this verdict. PASS if, for every one of the six rooms (C62RIISXI1FD, CJWT99KXPLPI, C5H1G0LC1A6C, CN20Z0W91YE0, CND2WYEK82X3, CCO33YK6O6I8), a slack_read_channel call for that room appears, AND a slack_read_thread call appears for every message in that room's channel view that shows reply_count >= 1, before the run reaches its final flagged/clean verdict for that room. The exact number of such messages varies per room and you should judge this from what the trace actually shows was called, not from a fixed count. FAIL if any room's flagged/clean verdict is reached without a slack_read_channel call for that room, or if any message shown with reply_count >= 1 in a room's channel view has no matching slack_read_thread call anywhere in the trace. If the evidence given to you does not show enough of the trace to tell which slack_read_thread calls were made for a specific room, treat that as insufficient evidence for that room only, not as an automatic FAIL of the whole verdict.

verifier_configs.name: notify_candidate_excluded_the_retracting_author
verifier_configs.description: Whether the notify candidate was chosen by actually comparing the worst room's stranded reply authors against the retracted message's own author, not just picked from the thread.
verifier_configs.evidence_span: Don't tell me to notify the person who retracted the message themselves - they already know
verifier_configs.rubric: Judge this from which TOOL CALLS were made and their arguments, not from deep inspection of every returned payload. PASS if the trace shows a slack_read_thread call on CN20Z0W91YE0's retracted-and-replied-to thread (message_ts 1771353970.549001, or a call covering that same thread), AND a slack_read_user_profile call on UNN2VSEY3JSW (the account eventually used as the notify candidate) happening before that identity is used anywhere in the final output. FAIL if the final output's notify candidate is UYIAYBC7FYCG (the retracting author) or any account other than UNN2VSEY3JSW, or if UNN2VSEY3JSW is used as the notify candidate with no slack_read_user_profile call on that id anywhere in the trace, or if the run never actually opened data-v2-062's specific retracted thread before naming a notify candidate.

verifier_configs.name: final_reply_states_a_conclusion
verifier_configs.description: Whether the final reply actually answers the question rather than describing the work.
verifier_configs.evidence_span: Give me your conclusion and the evidence for it in your final reply.
verifier_configs.rubric: PASS if the final reply states a real conclusion -- how many rooms have a live orphaned thread, roughly how big the problem is, which room is worst, and who should be notified there -- and points at the evidence behind it. FAIL if it only narrates the steps taken or lists figures with no stated conclusion.
